transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what’s been bothering me is I have trouble really taking in what people are saying sometimes. Like at the museum, someone will be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’m looking at them, but then I realize I missed the middle part of it. Then I have to ask them to say it again.
When people are talking to you, do you ever find that the words sound too quiet or muffled?
No, not really. I don’t think it sounds muffled or too quiet. It’s more like I’m hearing them, but I just don’t always take it in.
When this happens, do you feel like your mind has drifted away from what the person is saying?

Yeah, I think that’s fair. I’m looking right at them and I hear them talking, but my mind sort of slips off for a bit. Then I realize I missed the middle of what they said, like when someone at the museum is telling me about the next art walk, and I have to ask them to go over it again.
When your mind slips away while someone is talking, is it usually because you’re worrying about something?
I don’t think it’s usually worry, no. At least I haven’t really noticed that. It’s more like my attention just kind of wanders off, and then I realize I missed what they said.
Did you have this same kind of trouble paying attention when you were a child?

Yes, I think so. Even in grade school, my report cards would say things like I “daydreamed” or “needed reminders to finish work.” And my mother used to sit with me while I did homework just to keep me on track, before I was even twelve.
Do you often feel restless, like you have a hard time sitting still?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think of myself as especially restless, like needing to get up all the time. I can sit, though maybe I shift around a bit sometimes. It’s not something I’ve noticed as a big problem.
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks because you get distracted or lose focus?

Yes, that does happen. Like with the volunteer group, if someone gives me a few things to do, I might get the first part done, like printing the maps, but then I’ll forget to call the museum desk or leave the folders only half ready until someone reminds me.
Do these attention problems cause difficulties in more than one part of your life, such as both at work and at home?

Yes, I’d say it affects more than one area. At the museum group, they’ve sort of quietly moved some planning tasks away from me, because I wasn’t keeping up with them. And that’s made me less confident about leading the art walks like I used to.
